practice_span: I have worked with my father since I was eleven. It has now been forty-five years.
local_belonging_phrase: “The name of Kinnala is itself the mark of a Kinnala toy. They say our elders did this same work from the time of Hampi.”
ecological_input: Light soft wood used to come from the surrounding hills. Tamarind seed paste and the dry sun help the toys dry.
place_change: Cutting trees now needs permission, and there are fewer trees in the hills. Mining has raised the dust, and the boys go to Bengaluru.
emotion_about_place_change: “Without trees, where will toys come from? It feels like we must go and plant trees ourselves.”
teacher_name_relation: My father, Hanumappa Chitragar. My aunt taught me the painting.
teaching_memory: My father took a horse I had carved, closed his eyes and felt it. He said, “The horse isn't running.” After I bent the neck a little, he smiled.
remembered_phrase_gesture: “A toy's life is in its eyes.” As he said it, he held up a small brush between two fingers.
family_generations: My grandfather, my father, me. My son Manjunath carves, and my daughter-in-law Lakshmi paints. My grandson goes to school.
transmission_strength: The children of the house quickly learn small toys, birds and fruit.
transmission_weakness: The large festival deity figures and the old way of applying kitta. There isn't much demand for it now.
teaching_difficulty: Plastic toys are cheap. Learning takes years and pay isn't certain, so boys don't come.
primary_material: Light soft wood, tamarind seed paste, kitta (a mix of sawdust and paste), paints.
material_origin: Wood from Koppal and nearby hills. Tamarind seed from the village. Paints from the Hosapete market.
first_contact: I sat beside my father pounding tamarind seed. I still remember the sour smell of that paste.
material_special: This wood is light and soft to carve. So even a large figure can be carried by one person. Kitta makes the surface smooth.
material_in_hands: Good wood gives small shavings under the chisel and doesn't split. Kitta sticks to the finger but comes off easily.
material_feels_wrong: Green wood sticks to the chisel and cracks after drying. If kitta dries to powder, it doesn't hold.
correction_action: I dry green wood in the shade for months. If a crack comes, I fill it with kitta and give a coat of lime.
material_change_gain: Acrylic paint is bright, dries fast and lasts. Outside customers like it.
material_change_loss: The soft glow of the old paints made from stone and plants is gone. Few people know how to make them.
occasion_of_use: Figures for village fairs and deity festivals. Also toys for the Navaratri doll display.
sensory_scene: On the fair's night, the sound of drums, the smell of camphor, and a toy's eye glinting in the lamplight.
remembered_community_phrase: “When a Kinnala toy comes home, the child doesn't cry.” My grandmother used to say this.
special_vs_everyday: Everyday toys and fruit can be sold to anyone. A fair's deity figure is made only at the village's request.
special_object_rule: While making a deity figure we fast, and the eyes are painted on the last day. After that, the figure isn't kept at home.
not_for_sale_example: The goddess figure made for the village fair, and the old colour recipe from my grandfather's time.
why_protected: The figure belongs to the village, not to me. The recipe is the mark of our house. If it goes out, our work loses its value.
safer_alternative: Birds, horses and Dashavatara toys. Photos of them and video of the carving can be shown.
pride_moment: At Hampi Utsav a child would not let go of my toy and threw a tantrum. There were plastic toys right beside it.
recognition_by_others: The village elders called me to paint the eyes of the fair's figure. There is no greater honour.
loss_if_stopped: Light wood carving and the kitta method would go. It would be like the village losing its own name.
key_stakeholder_of_loss: The Chitragar families of Kinnala, and the surrounding villages that need figures for their fairs.
change_in_lifetime: Before, fair work was the most. Now it is small gift toys, and sales through government fairs.
artisan_initiated_change: I taught carving to my daughter-in-law and made a new small bird set. I am also inviting school children to workshops.
desired_keep: Hand carving, the kitta method, and the rules of the fair's figure.
desired_let_go: Waiting months for money after a fair, and the idea that women should only paint.
strength_anchor: My hand is steady at painting a toy's eyes. When I touch wood, I know whether it is right.
concern_anchor: Good wood is getting hard to find, and new boys are not coming to learn the work.
shareable_content: The carving method, the bird set, my name, the children's workshop.
private_content: The old colour recipe, the rites of the fair's figure, and the village's internal matters.
desired_change: Easier permission for wood, and schools asking for wooden toys instead of plastic.
desired_continuity: The fair's figure will be made in the village, by hand, by the old rules.
learning_story: Once in a hurry I made fifty toys from green wood. In the Delhi cold they all cracked. I gave the money back. Now I don't lift a chisel until the wood is dry.
emotional_story: In my father's last year his hand shook. He gave me the brush for the fair's figure. When I painted the eyes, he stood up and bowed.
clarification_story: Someone asked, this price for one bird? I gave it to them to lift. “So light?” they said. I told them that lightness takes six months of drying the wood.
outsider_misunderstanding: People believe this is only children's toys. These same hands make the goddess figure for the fair.
